active_verb_characteristics: Takes the final position in a sentence.

root_verb_principles: Root verbs are formed by common patterns of consonants.
They become meaningful upon taking vowels.

The source also discusses ma verbs and tä verbs.

examples: Rahel has a beautiful pair of shoes.

rules: Infinitives can be formed with mä....t or mä.... for consonant-initial stems.
If a stem begins with vowel sound a, mä can change to ma; these are called ma verbs in the source.
If the infinitive begins with mä/ma and ends with t, drop the prefix and suffix t to obtain the stem.
If the infinitive has mä/ma but does not end with t, drop the prefix and add ä at the end; the source notes exceptions.
If the infinitive has sixth-order ï between two consonants, change it to ä.
The source identifies mä verbs whose stems begin with a.
tä verbs start with tä and drop t in the infinitive; the source says t is retained in past tense but dropped in present/future and other expressions.

questions.question: What are the characteristics of active verbs in Amharic?
questions.answer: Active verbs express action, take the final position in a sentence, include subject, number, gender, object, tense, and a single verb can be a complete sentence depending on the context.

questions.question: How are root verbs formed in Amharic?
questions.answer: Root verbs in Amharic are formed by common patterns of consonants and become meaningful when they take on vowels.

ordinal_rules: If the cardinal ends in a vowel, add –ኛ–ňa.
